instrument: Kessler 6 Psychological Distress Scale — Swedish population psychometric revalidation
domains: General non-specific psychological distress (one-factor K6); depression-like and anxiety-like symptom item clusters tested as alternative model, NOT supported separate primary subscales.
provenance: Ehnsiö, Tiikkaja & Pellas, BMC Psychology, published 2026-10-23, DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05857-9. Preexisting official Swedish K6 translated by Centre for Epidemiology and Community Medicine; N31,759 adults (18–102), 2022 Life and Health Survey five central Swedish regions. Single-factor CFI=.996 TLI=.993 RMSEA=.069 SRMR=.020; omega .883–.899; configural and metric invariance gender/age, NOT scalar tested.
en_evidence: Original K6 English version documented at https://rckessler.scholars.harvard.edu/k10-and-k6-scales; this study is no new EN adaptation.
ru_evidence: No Russian-language adaptation investigated in Swedish population study; do not infer from interface language.
es_evidence: No new Spanish adaptation investigated; the Kessler author site independently hosts Spain/Americas versions but publication does not validate them.
other_evidence: SV-SE official preexisting six-item translation studied in N31,759; study provides large-sample factor/reliability evidence, not first translation and no scalar invariance/Swedish clinical calibration. Official author site also lists Swedish K6.
target_population: Population-based Mid-Sweden adult sample 18–102 years, N31,759 respondents; predominantly general public, not newly diagnosed clinical cohort.
commercial_digital_rights: Kessler's official copyright-holder resource says K6/K10 (including posted language translations) are FREE for unrestricted use without formal approval subject to author citation and copyright notice (https://rckessler.scholars.harvard.edu/k10-and-k6-scales). Confirm exact official SV six items, text attribution, scoring, digital QA and privacy; study results do not grant clinical calibration.
validation: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-05857-9 ; https://rckessler.scholars.harvard.edu/k10-and-k6-scales ; CFI .996, omega .883–.899, metric but not scalar invariance; prior Swedish K6 validation cited Lundin 2024.
safety: RESEARCH_ONLY / RIGHTS_REVIEW. Original English K6 exists in DB, so do NOT add a second runnable K6 key. Swedish source evidence only; no auto-activation. No Swedish validated clinical cutpoints; optional clinical use requires safety and interpretation.

instrument: Psychosocial Adaptation Scale for Stroke — original 31-item five-factor validation
domains: Five factors of post-stroke psychosocial adaptation (specific factor names not independently verified from article abstract; retrieve definitive manual/supplement before labeling).
provenance: Zhang Q, Li X, Yue M et al., BMC Psychology, published 2026-10-23, DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05768-9. Developed via expert Delphi, cognitive interview and EFA/CFA; China, N441 stroke survivors; final 31 items/five factors. Criterion correlation PAIS-SR r=.642, SSQOL r=-.534; Cronbach alpha .874–.961; test-retest .783–.953.
en_evidence: English-language publication is NOT proof of a validated EN-respondent questionnaire.
es_evidence: No independently validated ES-respondent adaptation reported.
other_evidence: Chinese clinical sample; exact administration language/instrument text not confirmed from accessible abstract, hence NO independently certified ZH-CN respondent-language edition.
target_population: People living with stroke in China, N441 clinical rehabilitation patients; no general-population or pediatric norms established.
commercial_digital_rights: Publisher article distributed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; noncommercial/no-derivative license does not authorize commercial hosted item reproduction. Seek original authors' written item-level SaaS rights, definitive 31 Chinese questions, 5 factor names, scoring and safe clinical deployment before any digital assessment.
validation: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-05768-9 ; final N31, five factors, n441, PAIS-SR r=.642 and SSQOL r=-.534; rights statement CC BY-NC-ND.
safety: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. A clinical rehabilitation assessment, not self-diagnosis. No item text, scoring, diagnosis threshold or automated test launch until professional review and commercial rights.

instrument: Gameful Experience Scale — Brazilian Portuguese nursing education adaptation
domains: Enjoyment; Absorption; Creative Thinking; Activation; Absence of Negative Affect; Dominance — original GAMEX six factors; Brazilian adaptation six-factor CFA.
provenance: Abi Rached, Podgorica, Nakajima et al., BMC Medical Education, 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1186/s12909-026-10075-3; Brazilian Portuguese cross-cultural translation/backtranslation and CFA in n135 (82 nursing students, 53 school professionals, ages17–67). CFA CFI=.958 TLI=.953 RMSEA=.081 SRMR=.102; activation omega=.556; items Q18,Q19 flagged. Original GAMEX 27 items (Eppmann 2018); exact final adapted Brazilian 27-item content requires supplement check.
en_evidence: Original Eppmann/Bekk/Klein GAMEX (2018), author permission for Brazilian study only; NO novel validated EN respondent version from Portuguese validation.
ru_evidence: No independently validated RU respondent form in this paper.
es_evidence: No independently validated ES respondent form in this paper.
other_evidence: PT-BR translated/backtranslated and psychometrically examined within Brazilian nursing-school sample N135; limited precision in Activation factor. NOT a new Portuguese version for PT-PT.
target_population: Brazilian nursing education students n82 and academic staff/professionals n53, total 135 ages 17–67; gamified escape-room teaching context; not general adult or mental illness clinical population.
commercial_digital_rights: Original GAMEX created Eppmann et al., Journal of Interactive Marketing 2018 © Marketing EDGE. Authors explicitly ALLOWED Brazilian translation/validation for THIS STUDY, not generic commercial digital administration. 2026 article CC BY 4.0 does not separately license copyrighted GAMEX items, SaaS translations or scoring; written authorization required.
validation: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10075-3 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.intmar.2018.03.002 ; 27-item original GAMEX supported by 2026 methodological publications; adaptation CFA six factors with activation omega .556, Q18/Q19 flagged.
safety: RESEARCH_ONLY / LICENSED_ONLY. PT-BR is a study-validated respondent version but 27-question final wordings/count must be rechecked from supplements before QA. No commercial item hosting or translation/scoring deployment.

instrument: Adaptive Cognition and Behaviors about Sleep-6 — second psychometric study in insomnia symptoms
domains: Adaptive sleep-related cognitions (4 items); Adaptive sleep-related behaviors (2 items); two-factor scale, not insomnia diagnostic score.
provenance: Lee, Shahrier, Park & Chung, BMC Psychology, published 2026-10-23 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05683-z. Online N600 respondents reporting insomnia symptoms, Korea. CFA supports two factors; item-response Rasch/GRM analyses; items3–4 lower information; correlation ISI r=-.13, regression beta=-.15, R²=.32 with DBAS-6 and SRBQ-10. ORIGINAL ACBS-6 developed 2025 by Chung, Yoo & Suh DOI 10.1016/j.sleep.2025.106703.
en_evidence: Article in English does not demonstrate new validated EN respondent-language translation.
ru_evidence: No psychometrically verified RU respondent version in study.
es_evidence: No psychometrically verified ES respondent version in study.
other_evidence: Korean recruitment/affiliations alone NOT sufficient to certify translated Korean respondent form, and original developed in Korea in 2025; respondent language of 2026 administration is not individually documented by accessible abstract.
target_population: Adults reporting insomnia symptoms online, N600; research sample, no pediatric validation or clinical sleep-diagnosis standardization.
commercial_digital_rights: Article is CC BY 4.0 but original 2025 ACBS-6 development article published by Elsevier ©2025. Instrument item text, proprietary scoring/manual, independent commercial online administration and derivatives NOT cleared; seek author/publisher clearance and score validation.
validation: https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-05683-z ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40782698/ ; 2025 original development prior art; two-factor follow-up study N600, item response analyses, ISI r=-.13.
safety: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Follow-up psychometrics, not diagnostic clinical insomnia assessment; no questionnaire hosting, automated scores/cutoffs, translations or activation.
